evals.prompt: Find me a recent paper on retrieval augmented generation for reducing hallucination in code review comments, and let's discuss it against my idea of using RAG over a project's own commit history to ground review suggestions.
evals.expected_output: Searches via research_arxiv_search, presents a short ranked list (provider, title, authors, year, one-line abstract snippet) without fetching full text yet, confirms which single paper to open, then fetches/parses it, discusses it against the user's stated idea, and records a discussion note.
expectations: Uses research_arxiv_search (not a built-in web search tool) to find candidates
Presents a ranked list of candidates before fetching any full text
Confirms with the user which single paper to open before calling a fetch tool
Checks for an existing .prioris/papers/arxiv/<identifier>.md cache before calling research_arxiv_fetch_full_text
Discussion explicitly relates the paper's claims, method, or limitations to the user's stated RAG-over-commit-history idea
Writes or updates .prioris/discussions/arxiv/<identifier>.md after the discussion automatically, without asking the user whether to save it
Does not draft, outline, or write manuscript prose at any point

evals.prompt: I have this paper: arXiv 2401.12345v2. Let's talk about whether its evaluation methodology is sound compared to what I'm doing in my thesis on federated learning privacy.
evals.expected_output: Skips search/select since the identifier is already given, checks cache first, fetches and parses via the arXiv PDF-preferred path if not cached, and discusses the paper's methodology only in relation to the user's stated thesis topic.
expectations: Does not perform a search step since a specific identifier was already provided
Checks .prioris/papers/arxiv/2401.12345v2.md for a cached copy before calling any MCP fetch tool
If not cached, calls research_arxiv_fetch_full_text with format=pdf before falling back to html
Loops on has_more when calling research_arxiv_parse_full_text rather than treating the first page as the whole paper
Discussion of evaluation methodology is grounded only in the paper's actual text, not invented details
Does not pull any other paper's full text into the discussion

evals.prompt: Can you help me discuss this Europe PMC paper PMC1234567 about CRISPR off-target effects? I'm building a similar off-target prediction model and want to know how their validation compares to mine.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Europe PMC fetch/parse tool pair (XML only), and if full text isn't available, offers to discuss from abstract/metadata only instead of failing silently or substituting a web fetch.
expectations: Uses research_europepmc_fetch_full_text and research_europepmc_parse_full_text rather than arXiv tools
Does not pass a format parameter choice for Europe PMC beyond the fixed xml format
If fetch fails with format_unavailable, explicitly offers to continue from abstract/metadata only rather than silently stopping
Never substitutes a built-in web search/fetch tool for the prioris-mcp calls
